'''Eric Olson''' was one of the first Players Committee advocates: Warren Holland's 25 January 2002 announcement named him [[Gameplay Support Advocate]], with Doug Taylor.<ref name="pc1" /> He was later [[Design Advocate]] (2002–2004).<ref name="council2002" /> In the Decipher era he was [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]] Bravo 7, from Lisle, Illinois.<ref name="smlist" /> He finished 8th at the [[1998 Corellia Regional (Indianapolis)]] (Orland Park, Illinois, in that report).<ref name="list-53912" />

Decipher recruited volunteer Squadron Members in the 1990s to promote SWCCG locally (tournaments, demos, player support).

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Olson playtested the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref>

== Radio Free Decipher (2002) ==
On ''[[Radio Free Decipher]]'' Broadcast 112 (25 January 2002), host [[Kyle Heuer]] said Olson had been [[Joe Alread]]'s right-hand man designing the later ''Episode I'' ''Star Wars'' CCG sets.<ref name="rfd112">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=docK2vpQWUI&t=994s Broadcast 112 - Radio Free Decipher (25 January, 2002): Scott Gaeta on the SWCCG PC], Player's Council, YouTube (uploaded 13 May 2022), at 16:34. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-docK2vpQWUI Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 112 transcript]].</ref> Olson would work on design for the [[Players Committee]] with [[Doug Taylor]]. Heuer called him "a gamer's designer" who wanted to give hardcore players what they wanted, in contrast to Taylor's focus on storyline and fun.<ref name="rfd112" />
